Clayton Tucker

Democratic candidate for Commissioner of Agriculture, Texas

Rancher on his family's ranch in Lampasas; fair trade organizer for the Trade Justice Education Fund; Secretary of the Texas Farmers Union

Clayton Tucker, 35, is a fifth-generation Texan from Lampasas who works on his family's RX Ranch and is Secretary of the Texas Farmers Union. He ran unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary and won the nomination with about 1.92 million votes. He faces Republican Nate Sheets in the November 3, 2026 general election for Texas Commissioner of Agriculture, an open seat after incumbent Sid Miller lost the Republican primary.

Where Tucker stands

Rural economy
Proposes issuing 'Ag Impact Studies' on Day 1 that would require data centers to disclose their water and power use. Also proposes 'Ag Development Districts' so local communities can push back against data center projects.
Food quality and children's health
Proposes requiring that public school lunches be made and processed in Texas. Supports removing harmful chemicals from food.
Food quality and children's health
Supports stopping the spread of microplastics and regulating chemicals such as PFAS.
Support for agricultural producers
Supports breaking up corporate monopolies in agriculture, naming companies such as Tyson Foods and John Deere. Wants to make it easier for young farmers to stay in agriculture and to preserve family farms.
Support for agricultural producers
Lists lowering the cost of food among his campaign priorities.
Agency reform
Says his focus as commissioner would be removing the 'thievin elite' from the department and staying out of cultural fights.
Candidate eligibility
His attorneys asked the Texas GOP to review whether Sheets meets the legal qualifications for the office. Tucker argues beekeeping does not count under the ag code, though he says he would probably support changing the law to include it.

Background

  • Grew up working on his family's RX Ranch in Lampasas; moved back in 2016 to help run it
  • Worked as a water and agriculture researcher for the National Science Foundation
  • Worked for an environmental compliance firm in Shanghai; taught kindergarten in Taipei
  • Led a political organization founded by former Agriculture Commissioner Jim Hightower; former Our Revolution organizer
  • Ran unsuccessfully for the Texas Senate in 2020
  • Co-founder of the Texas Grassroots Alliance
  • Secretary of the Texas Farmers Union
  • Fair trade organizer for the Trade Justice Education Fund
  • Unopposed Democratic nominee for Texas Agriculture Commissioner, March 3, 2026 primary
